latest_release.name: TensorFold 1.3.6
latest_release.body:
# TensorFold 1.3.6

1.3.6 brings exact CUDA TFQ3 serving and speculative drafting to Qwen3.8-27B, GLM-5.3-Flash and Flash Next. It also adds LFM3-VL images on Metal, full GLM-5.3 on CUDA, more LFM3 formats and SenseNova-Loop MLX-affine checkpoints, alongside substantial Inkling 2 speedups and broader prompt-cache controls. A stable release now publishes checked Linux amd64 and arm64 container images (#4986, #1502, #4900, #1634, #1508, #4415, #3857).

## CUDA TFQ3

- **Qwen3.8-27B, GLM-5.3-Flash and Flash Next:** CUDA serves 3/4/5-bit 2D-AffineCoset TFQ3 checkpoints with randomized 2D FWHT-128. Qwen3.8-27B supports DFlash2 and DSpine drafting from BF16 or MLX bases, GLM-5.3-Flash supports MTP and DFlash2, and Flash Next supports its routed TFQ3 layers and MTP drafter alongside MLX PLE checkpoints. Shared dense and Tensor Core kernels provide bit-exact speculative verification; non-TFQ3 checkpoints keep their existing paths (#4986).
- **Flash Next top-5 checkpoints:** a checkpoint with a 1280-wide shared expert loads those projections at their real width rather than 640; top-10/640 checkpoints are unchanged. The optional Inkling 2 EXL3 pack-test path, `TF_INKLING2_EXL3_DIR`, is registered and documented (#5228).

## Speed

- **Inkling 2 Mini on Metal:** tensor-unit expert and loop-gate projections make 2K-token prompts about 1.95x faster on M5, with tokens unchanged (#5144). Multi-row logits use coalesced 32-wide vocabulary tiles, making four-stream decode about 3.5% faster on M3 Ultra and 4.5% on M5 with byte-equal results (#5135). Coalesced NVFP4 and MXFP8 expert loads and stable SIMD combining preserve every output bit (#5150). Cached inverse RMS and fused partial updates make single-stream decode about 4% faster on M3 and M5 (#5001).
- **More Inkling 2 Metal gains:** grouped routed-expert reads give about 1.9x prompt fill and 15-19% faster four-stream decode on M5 Ultra (#4995). Dense power-of-two matvec kernels gain about 3.6% on M3 Ultra (#4998), fused relative-bias attention makes decode about 3-7% faster on M3 Ultra (#5000), and 16-byte decode reads with parallel router selection move one-stream M4 Pro decode from 9.3 to 20.9 tok/s (#4919).
- **Inkling 2 drafting and prefill:** the reworked DSpark drafter batches streams, removes attention score scratch and uses a two-pass GPU top-k while preserving plain and drafted output bits (#4699). On M1 to M4, simdgroup prompt kernels cut a cold 2,048-token prompt from 146 s to 9.7 s on M4 Pro with identical greedy output (#4756). Tree-shaped verification windows now run with output bits equal to the linear path (#5011).
- **Inkling 2 Mini on CUDA:** the staged QKV decode projection reaches 5.6 to 6.4 tok/s on GB10 with identical bits (#4718). Sharing one forward pass across concurrent streams makes four-stream decode about 2.7-3.4x faster, with each stream's tokens equal to its solo run (#4786).
- **CUDA sampling:** grouped radix probes replace bit-by-bit top-p cutoff searches. At `top_p=0.95`, a row takes 279-286 us instead of 427-515 us on GB10; every draw, probability and token is unchanged (#4691).
- **Vision on Metal:** BF16 attention scores and probabilities halve Inkling 2 image-tower score traffic with byte-identical answers (#5120). Its two FP32 attention dots also use 64 x 64 tiles with byte-identical answers (#5119).
- **Other exact work:** Ling-3.0-tiny attention on ARM CPUs is about 10% faster at one and four threads with unchanged tokens and logits (#5071). GLM's Metal DFlash2 draft decode fuses projections and reads packed rows without changing verified tokens (#4258). Metal EXL3 adds exact multi-row projections and a fused gate/up epilogue (#5054), and MiniMax-H3-Image reads ahead only the tensors it uses with mapped BF16 bytes and decoder conversion unchanged (#4909).

## New models, formats and guides

Help Support TensorFold · @tensorfold_dev on X

# TensorFold TensorFold serves language models from a Zig binary on Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs. The engine reads checkpoints, tokenizes requests and runs Metal or CUDA kernels directly. Serving needs no Python or MLX installation. Building with a coding agent? Have it load the [contributor skill](docs/recipes/SKILL.md) and follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-with-agents). ## Quick start Start with Qwen3.5-2B, a small 4-bit checkpoint. The commands below download its pinned revision, then serve it as `local-model`. Model weights have their own licenses. ### Mac with Apple Silicon Install with Homebrew, then start the server: ```sh brew install ashhart/tensorfold/tensorfold tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3 tensorfold serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit --name local-model --context 8192 --no-thinking ``` ### Linux with an NVIDIA GPU Needs glibc 2.28 or newer and NVIDIA driver R580 or newer (CUDA 13.0). The [run guide](docs/run-guide.md#platform-setup) lists the archive's requirements; Windows has [its own guide](docs/WINDOWS.md). ```sh V=1.3.6 case "$(uname -m)" in aarch64|arm64) PLATFORM=linux-aarch64 ;; x86_64) PLATFORM=linux-x86_64 ;; *) echo 'No release archive for this CPU' >&2; exit 1 ;; esac curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" sha256sum -c "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" tar -xzf "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" export PATH="$PWD/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM/bin:$PATH" tensorfold() { command tensorfold-native "$@"; } tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3 tensorfold serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit --name local-model --context 8192 --no-thinking ``` ### Send a request Leave the server running. In another terminal, on either platform: ```sh curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"local-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello in one sentence."}],"max_tokens":128,"temperature":0}' ``` The API also serves completions, Responses and Anthropic Messages. `/v1/models` lists the served name. To talk to a model in the terminal in one command, `tensorfold chat MODEL` starts the server itself, streams each reply and stops the server when the chat ends; `/help` lists the chat's commands, and `/bye` or Ctrl-D ends it: ```sh tensorfold chat mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit ``` With the server above still running, `tensorfold chat --url http://127.0.0.1:8080` chats with it instead, and `echo "Say hello." | tensorfold chat --url http://127.0.0.1:8080` prints one reply for a script. See [the chat command](docs/chat.md) for its flags and the serve flags it passes on. ## Docs - [Run guide](docs/run-guide.md): platform setup, requests, parallel requests, exact decoding, context compaction, Cortheon mode, every serve flag, the Mac app and TensorFold Starlight. - [Supported models](docs/supported-models.md): which checkpoints run on which machines, models on disk and model discovery. - [Living Weights (experimental)](docs/living-weights.md): teach a running model new facts in its own weights. - [Installation runbook](RUNBOOK.md): macOS and CUDA installation, paired Metal serving and troubleshooting. - [Windows](docs/WINDOWS.md), [TensorFold Web](docs/web.md) and [the Mac app](app/README.md). - [API](docs/api.md), [Cortheon mode](docs/cortheon.md) and [known issues](docs/known-issues.md). - [Claude Code](docs/claude-code.md): point it at a local server, name its model, and keep its prompt prefix cacheable. - [Evaluating TensorFold](docs/evaluating.md) and [community benchmarks](docs/community-benchmarks.md). - [Usable memory profiles](docs/memory-profiling.md): how to record applied budgets, context, cache state and process peaks. - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): ATC and agents, builds, tests and the exactness and performance gates. - [Changes](CHANGELOG.md), [1.0.0 release notes](docs/release-notes-1.0.0.md) and [the Zig engine preview](docs/zig-preview.md). - TensorFold is Apache-2.0: [LICENSE](LICENSE), [NOTICE](NOTICE), [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Contributors
